verdict.summary: CrowdStrike's Q2 FY27 report shows Falcon still taking wallet share: revenue rose 26% to $1.47B, ending ARR reached $5.84B and net-new ARR was $332.8M. Free cash flow was $377.4M. The catch is accounting quality: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.01 against non-GAAP EPS of $0.31, and GAAP operating income remained negative after recurring exclusions. Management now guides FY27 revenue to $5.991B-$6.011B and ending ARR to $6.603B-$6.612B. At 37.2x guided revenue and a 0.7% annualized FCF yield, ARR durability must remain exceptional. A completed 15-minute close above $228.49 activates the setup; $216.4649 is the pre-earnings pivot stop, while $252.06 and $254.83 are measured moves from dated ranges. AI identity growth helps, but competition and July 2024 incident liability still constrain quality.

business.overview:
CrowdStrike sells cloud subscriptions to the Falcon platform, spanning endpoint, identity, cloud workload, log management, managed detection and security operations. Revenue is driven by customer count, module adoption, renewal and expansion, best tracked through ARR and net-new ARR.

AI creates two paid channels: customers need to secure more machine identities and AI workloads, while Falcon uses its telemetry to automate detection and response. The economic test is whether those products increase modules and net-new ARR, not whether management mentions agents.

The model breaks through a platform outage, missed detections, pricing pressure or slower expansion. Stock compensation and incident-related costs can keep GAAP economics far below the non-GAAP presentation even while free cash flow remains strong.

CrowdStrike must turn net-new ARR into reported operating profit after incident costs and equity compensation. Platform breadth matters only if release controls, retention and diluted-share cash generation improve together.
business.moat: Falcon's moat is the combination of a single cloud-native sensor, broad security telemetry, threat intelligence and a growing module marketplace. Consolidation lowers deployment friction, but Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks and specialist vendors can bundle aggressively; the moat must show up in ARR retention and module expansion.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 FY27 revenue was $1.471B (+26%), ending ARR $5.84B (+25%) and net-new ARR $332.8M; free cash flow was $377.4M. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.01 versus $0.31 non-GAAP. Management guided Q3 ARR to $6.184B-$6.188B, revenue to $1.523B-$1.529B and non-GAAP operating income to $372.7M-$375.9M. FY27 guidance is ARR of $6.603B-$6.612B, revenue of $5.991B-$6.011B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.25-$1.26 on 1.044B diluted shares. The company did not reconcile forward non-GAAP measures where excluded items cannot be predicted, and the next earnings date is not confirmed by the reviewed release.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: CrowdStrike reported 1,023,934,842 basic shares outstanding on August 20, 2026 and 1,044,469,000 diluted weighted-average shares for Q2 FY27. The quarterly diluted average is the minimum calculable denominator; a current theoretical fully diluted count is unavailable because unvested and anti-dilutive awards are not reconciled into a point-in-time total. CrowdStrike has no reviewed ATM or prospectus-based equity issuance in the current filing set. Employee equity and related payroll taxes remain the practical dilution channel and help explain the GAAP/non-GAAP gap. Cash of $4.55B exceeds $821M of debt, so external equity is not required for liquidity.
